the mismatch: 'in' is mewn before an indefinite noun, yn before a definite one
example: mewn amser byr vs yn y tŷ bwyta
why there is no support: the intro says only 'in a short time is mewn amser byr'; no contrast with the yn the learner already has

the mismatch: dy (your) takes soft mutation, fy (my) takes nasal; the same noun shows up in three shapes
example: dy Gymraeg, dy fam, dy lyfr, dy frawd vs fy mam, fy mrawd, fy nhad
why there is no support: dy chwaer (the taught LEGO) hides the mutation; the only side-by-side is S0115L01B02 dy fam … fy mam i, with no explanation

the mismatch: a direct object soft-mutates after a short-form verb and its subject
example: ges i wydrad (gwydrad taught); ddudodd fy mam rywbeth (S0115L02B04)
why there is no support: the first visible case; the LEGOs carry the radical forms

the mismatch: the object 'it' is gendered and has several constructions: ei + soft (masc) / ei + radical + hi (fem) / verbnoun + fo/hi
example: wnes i ei fwynhau; wnes i ei mwynhau; wnes i ei gwylio hi; wnest ti wylio hi; wylio fo
why there is no support: English 'it' gives no clue and no antecedent is named; see the two-targets finding

the mismatch: a bod clause carries no tense: English 'that it WAS' is still fod o
example: ddudodd o wrthaf fi fod o ar y teledu
why there is no support: the learner was given 'was' = oedd (oedd o / oedd yn braf), and nothing tells them it does not apply after 'that'

the mismatch: 'it was' with or without a pronoun
example: oedd o ar y teledu vs oedd yn braf / oedd yn ddiddorol
why there is no support: nothing tells the learner when the o appears

the mismatch: tell + noun is deud wrth + (mutated) noun; tell + pronoun is a conjugated preposition
example: ddeud wrth fy mam, deud wrth bawb vs deud wrthaf fi / wrthot ti
why there is no support: bare wrth is never taught; the seed itself needs it

the mismatch: 'that he' = fod o, 'that she' = bod hi (traces of ei fod / ei bod); 'that I/you' = bo’ fi/ti
example: ddudodd fy mam bod hi’n gweithio vs ddudodd hi fod o isio (U03)
why there is no support: the LEGOs S0080L02 'she said that | … bod' and S0081L01 '… fod o' imply that the form belongs to the speaker, not to the clause subject; U03 breaks that reading silently

the mismatch: a negative reported clause uses na instead of bod
example: ddudodd dy fam wrthaf fi na ddylwn i ddim deud …
why there is no support: never taught; the learner’s only 'that' is bo’/bod; it also breaks at S0118L01B01 (na dydy)

the mismatch: past-tense yes/no answers are do / naddo, not a repeat of the verb
example: naddo, wnes i wylio …
why there is no support: do was met only fused into chunks (do, ges i; do, wnes i …); naddo is unannounced

the mismatch: neb (nobody) needs a negative verb: 'nobody wants' = does neb isio
example: does neb angen deud wrthaf fi
why there is no support: only the intro example carries does; no LEGO teaches it

the mismatch: digon goes BEFORE the adjective, and mutates after yn
example: I’m happy enough | dw i’n ddigon hapus
why there is no support: English order is reversed; nothing frames it

the mismatch: 'something to eat' can be rhywbeth i’w fwyta: 'w (its) plus soft mutation, a pronoun English does not have
example: rhywbeth i’w fwyta / gormod i’w fwyta vs digon i fwyta / rhywbeth i yfed
why there is no support: 'w is never taught, and both shapes alternate with the same English

the mismatch: 'yes' depends on the question: yndw answers wyt ti …? (present), do answers a past question
example: are you ready? yndw, dw i’n barod vs did you enjoy it? do, wnes i …
why there is no support: yndw comes inside a chunk and do only ever inside chunks; nothing sets them side by side

the mismatch: 'that' before a future is y + short-form verb, not bod
example: mae’n bosib y wela i chdi yno; mae’n bwysig cofio y wela i chdi yno
why there is no support: y was never a LEGO; the learner’s 'that' is bo’/bod (and an untaught na)

the mismatch: â (as, with) causes aspirate mutation
example: cymaint â phosib (posib / mae’n bosib)
why there is no support: yr un peth â fy nhad shows nothing; the seed needs phosib straight away

the mismatch: 'as X as' is mor X â (mor + soft mutation)
example: mor aml â phosib
why there is no support: mor was met only in pa mor hir? (how long?); the LEGO is yn aml

the mismatch: 'wait for X' is aros am X, but 'wait for me to do' is aros i mi + soft verbnoun
example: aros am dy fam vs paid ag aros i mi ddechrau
why there is no support: only the am form is taught; the i mi form is supported weakly by isio i mi helpu

the mismatch: a negative short past puts an aspirate on c/p/t and a soft mutation on the rest
example: chlywes i ddim, chest ti ddim vs clywes i, gest ti; wnes i ddim, weles i
why there is no support: the intro gives the analytic alternative but no pattern; gest ti → chest ti ddim changes the first letter twice

the mismatch: an identification question puts the noun first: ai + noun + ydy + subject
example: are those your children? ai eich plant chi ydy rheina?
why there is no support: the LEGO and the intro teach ydy rheina? as plain verb-first; ai is never taught

the mismatch: a plural pronoun takes maen (maen nhw), but a plural noun subject takes singular mae
example: maen nhw’n hapus vs mae rhai pobl yn meddwl
why there is no support: maen nhw arrives 13 seeds after mae rhai pobl, with one phrase and no contrast

the mismatch: possession with gan: the possessed noun soft-mutates after oes gynnoch chi / mae gynnon ni, but not after ddim
example: oes gynnoch chi blant? mae gynnon ni ferch / fab / ddau hogyn vs na, sgynnon ni ddim plant / merch / mab
why there is no support: mae gen i ffrind (ff does not mutate) was the only model; no intro mentions it and the radical/mutated pair turns on ddim

the mismatch: a third yes/no system: an oes question is answered oes / nag oes (cut to na), and oes needs an indefinite subject
example: oes gynnoch chi blant? oes, mae gynnon ni … / na, sgynnon ni ddim …; misuse at S0154L02U04 oes gynnoch chi’r fenga?
why there is no support: yndw and do were the answers so far; the intro hides nag oes behind na, which the learner already uses for 'no' generally

the mismatch: i and am conjugate with pronouns like wrth: i + nhw = iddyn nhw, am + chi = amdanoch chi, am + fi = amdanaf fi
example: gofyn iddyn nhw; aros amdanoch chi (S0166L01B05); aros amdanaf fi (S0167L01U04)
why there is no support: only gofyn i ti / aros am + noun were taught; the 114 wrth line covers wrth alone

the mismatch: two is dau (masc) / dwy (fem); after y both soft-mutate (y ddau, y ddwy), and so do they after mae gynnon ni
example: dwy hogan, dau hogyn, mae’r ddwy hogan, y ddau hogyn, mae gynnon ni ddau hogyn
why there is no support: the intro says 'dau or dwy' with no rule or example of which goes with which

the mismatch: a definite predicate ('X is the Y') takes identification order: subject first, then ydy
example: yr hogan ydy’r fenga; yr hogyn ydy’r fenga
why there is no support: mae … yn is the learner's only 'is'; ai … ydy rheina? (138) was a question and was itself taught as verb-first

the mismatch: ei 'her' adds h- to a vowel and aspirates c/p/t; ei 'his' soft-mutates (vowels unchanged)
example: yn ei hugeiniau / yn ei ugeiniau; yn ei dridegau / yn ei thridegau
why there is no support: one form of each is taught with no his/her contrast; the siblings are then demanded (S0158L02B04, B07)

the mismatch: the chi register is a second verb paradigm: dach / ydach chi, wnaethoch / gaethoch chi, oeddach chi, peidiwch
example: be’ dach chi’n …; gaethoch chi amser da?; oeddach chi isio; peidiwch ag aros
why there is no support: only oes gynnoch chi (147) and dach chi ddim yn edrych (156) are LEGOs; the rest arrive in phrases

the mismatch: possession of a DEFINITE noun reverses the order: the thing comes first, then gan (bod ein plant gynnon ni), against mae gynnon ni blant for an indefinite one
example: maen nhw isio i ni wneud yn siŵr bod ein plant gynnon ni
why there is no support: only the indefinite order (oes gynnoch chi …? / mae gynnon ni …) was ever modelled

the mismatch: 'about it' is a conjugated am that carries gender: amdani (feminine or abstract 'it'), amdano fo (masculine), chosen by the noun the 'it' stands for
example: maen nhw’n meddwl amdani vs y llyfr ’na oeddan ni’n siarad amdano fo (seed 196)
why there is no support: neither is ever a LEGO, and English 'about it' gives no clue to the gender

the mismatch: conditional 'we would' is bydden ni; byddan / fyddan ni is the future 'we will', yet the course has used fyddan for 'would' since 151
example: bydden ni’n licio vs fyddan ni ddim isio
why there is no support: the only conditional model was byddai fo (3rd singular); the we-forms are never set side by side

the mismatch: a relative clause that ends in a preposition has no 'that' word and ends with a conjugated preposition
example: wnest ti ddarllen y llyfr ’na oeddan ni’n siarad amdano fo?
why there is no support: the seed needs it, and no LEGO or phrase models it first

the mismatch: the English simple past splits two ways: states (think, want, know) take the imperfect, events (watch, read, have) take the short past
example: what did you think? be’ oeddat ti’n meddwl? vs did you watch? wnest ti wylio?; oeddan ni isio, doeddan ni ddim yn gwybod vs gest ti?
why there is no support: each arrives as its own chunk; nothing tells the learner which English 'did you' takes which form
